clues: This large city in the north of Spain sits just south of the Bay of Biscay. It lies where a river meets the sea in a wide mouth.
Sea air and low cloud from the bay keep summers mild in this city. Rain falls a lot here, and bright sun is rare through the year.
It was founded in the late years of the twelve hundreds by Diego López V de Haro. He led a strong clan and made this a trade hub.
Its famed football club fields only Basque players, by long choice and pride. Fans treat that strict rule as a badge of who they are.
The famed Guggenheim Museum is the top sight in this city. It sparked a fresh start for the old port and trade town.
